name: Track Circuit
description: The definition of a lap: an ordered checkpoint sequence laid over a spline, the radius that counts as crossing each gate, and the validation that decides whether a lap counts. It exists because 'who is winning' is only computable once 'what progress means' is nailed down, and progress on a circuit is gate order, not distance to a finish line. This component owns gate order, lap counting, and wrong-way or gate-skip detection — reported as world.lapInvalidated rather than enforced physically, because whether a skipped gate means respawn, penalty, or disqualification is a race-rules decision made above it. It does not own grid placement, standings, or podium logic, and it deliberately borrows timing from utility.timer_system instead of keeping a private clock, so replays, ghosts, and race control all read the same time. Race start and reset arrive as named commands via utility.command_bus rather than bespoke inputs.

inputs.name: checkpointPositions
inputs.description: Ordered gate positions along the spline. Order is the contract: gates must be crossed in sequence for a lap to validate.

inputs.name: lapCount
inputs.description: Laps required to finish the race. world.raceFinished fires when the first racer completes this count.

inputs.name: checkpointRadius
inputs.description: Distance from a gate that counts as crossing it. Wide gates forgive arcade lines; tight gates reward precision and make cutting detectable.

inputs.name: allowCheckpointSkip
inputs.description: When false, crossing gate N+1 before gate N invalidates the lap. Rally-style point-to-point stages may set this true and validate only gate order overall.

outputs.name: trackLength
outputs.description: Spline length in world units, exposed so pacing systems such as utility.rubber_band_ai can reason in seconds rather than units.

outputs.name: leaderLap
outputs.description: Highest validated lap among tracked racers. Standings UI derives position from lap plus last checkpoint, both readable here.
